name: ScrollArea
description: A scrolling box with thin overlay scrollbars that look the same on every platform and theme. Scrolling itself stays native (wheel, touch, keyboard); the scrollbars can also be dragged, and a press on a gutter pages.

props.name: actionsRef
props.type: ((instance: ScrollAreaActions | null) => void | (() => void | { [UNDEFINED_VOID_ONLY]: never; }) | DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES[keyof DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES]) | RefObject<ScrollAreaActions | null>
props.description: Methods to scroll from code that the container doesn't have natively.

props.name: children
props.description: The scrolling content, in ScrollArea's own container. Not read with `renderContainer`.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class of ScrollArea's own container; with `sticky` the same element as the root.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Style of ScrollArea's own container.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Class of a content element around `children`, inside the container: put padding here, so the scrollbars stay at the edges. Only with it, `contentStyle` or `fade` (sticky) is there one.

props.name: contentRef
props.description: An element whose size is the content's, watched for size changes (such as a hidden mirror of a textarea's text). Without it each element child of the container is watched, and children added or removed.

props.name: contentStyle
props.description: Style of the content element; renders it, as `contentClassName` does.

props.name: fade
props.description: Fade the content out toward an edge that has more past it. The scrollbars don't fade.

props.name: guttersPosition
props.description: Where the gutters go: inside the container (`sticky`, the default) or beside it in a frame (`absolute`).

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the scrollbars stay after scrolling stops, in ms. At least 100 with `trigger="scroll"`.

props.name: onEdgeChange
props.description: Called when the area reaches or leaves an edge, and after mounting when the content overflows.

props.name: onScroll
props.description: The container's scroll events.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The directions the area scrolls in. Content too wide for a vertical area is cut off.

props.name: overscroll
props.description: What a scroll that reaches the end does: stop there with no bounce (`none`, the default), stop there but let Mac trackpads and iOS bounce the area (`contain`), or carry on to the page behind (`auto`, which leaves the container's own `overscroll-behavior` alone). Only in the directions the area overflows right now.

props.name: railInset
props.description: Room in px the scrollbars keep clear at each end, such as a sticky header's height, so they don't run over it. Also settable in CSS, on the root: `--r-scroll-area-rail-inset-{top,bottom,left,right}`, which don't inherit.

props.name: renderContainer
props.description: Renders the container yourself, in place of ScrollArea's `<div>`: a `<textarea>`, a list, another component's own scroller (VirtualList's `domRef`). Put the binding on the element that scrolls and `<ScrollAreaGutters />` where `guttersPosition` says: as its first child (`sticky`) or right after it (`absolute`, inside the frame ScrollArea renders around what this returns). ScrollArea listens to the container's scroll itself. The demo's `useContainer`.

props.name: rootRef
props.type: ((instance: HTMLDivElement | null) => void | (() => void | { [UNDEFINED_VOID_ONLY]: never; }) | DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES[keyof DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES]) | RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>
props.description: The root: the container itself (`sticky`) or the frame (`absolute`).

props.name: size
props.description: Thumb thickness: `small` is 5px, `medium` 7px; both grow while pointed at or dragged.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description: The container's: by default `0` while there is something to scroll.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the scrollbars show. They always show while scrolling or dragging.

name: ScrollAreaContent
description: An optional box around the content, inside the container (the demo's `ScrollAreaResizableContent`): for padding, so the scrollbars stay at the edges, or a layout of the content's own. In a horizontal (or `both`) area it is as wide as its widest child. It is watched for size changes like any child of the container.

name: ScrollAreaTextarea
description: A native `<textarea>` with ScrollArea's overlay scrollbar: ScrollArea with `guttersPosition="absolute"` and the textarea as its container (it can't hold children), the gutters beside it in the frame, as in the demo's textarea example. Its own `scrollHeight` is the content size: it is measured on every input and render, and when the box resizes. Native props, `ref`, `className`, `style` and `onScroll` go to the textarea; `wrapperClassName` and `wrapperStyle` to the frame.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the scrollbar stays after scrolling stops, as on ScrollArea.

props.name: overscroll
props.description: Whether a scroll that reaches the end carries on to the page, as on ScrollArea.

props.name: size
props.description: Thumb thickness, as on ScrollArea.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the scrollbar shows, as on ScrollArea.

props.name: wrapperClassName
props.description: Class of the root that holds the textarea and its scrollbar.

props.name: wrapperStyle
props.description: Style of the root; size the textarea itself with `className` / `style`.
